# Connection support across the four cores

What each of the four cores can be configured to do, at the versions below, in one place. The two questions this document exists to keep apart are *what a core supports* and *what a benchmark measured*: a core can support a connection that no loopback benchmark will ever exercise, and a benchmark can measure a connection that no user will ever configure.

## Versions

| Project | Version | Source | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Zray (this workspace)](https://github.com/zeghostwriter/ZeroNet) | `0.1.0` | built from this checkout | built from the checkout under test |
| [Xray-core](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core) | `v26.3.27` | release asset or source tag | last release with full release notes; later tags are prereleases |
| [sing-box](https://github.com/SagerNet/sing-box) | `1.14.2` | release asset or source tag | current stable line; a 1.15.0 alpha is in progress |
| [xray-rust](https://github.com/aimalygin/xray-rust) | `v0.7.0` | release asset or source tag | source only; no prebuilt binaries are published |

A capability table is only true of a version. The benchmark report records the version string and the SHA-256 of every binary it actually ran; if the two disagree, the binary is the truth and this table is out of date.

## Legend

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `yes` | supported at the pinned version |
| `partial` | supported with a documented restriction |
| `deprecated` | still works; the project directs new configurations elsewhere |
| `alpha` / `prerelease` | present in an alpha or unreleased line, not in the pinned version |
| `removed` | the project reports the feature as removed |
| `no` | not supported |
| `n-a` | the concept does not exist in that project's configuration model |

A cell in the tables below is a statement about what a project can be
**configured** to do. It is not a statement about what the benchmark in
`docs/benchmarks` measures: most of this surface cannot be reached by a
single-process client on loopback, which is precisely why it is written down
here instead of being left to be discovered.

## Charts

Two views of the same data, generated alongside a benchmark run and also
standalone:

- `charts/protocol-transport-grid.png` -- one panel per core, protocol against
  transport, `1.00` where the core can be configured for that combination and
  `0.00` where it cannot. The empty cells are the gaps.
- `charts/capability-surface.png` -- every row of these tables, all four cores,
  on one scale, so a column can be read top to bottom.

## Client protocol

| Feature | Zray (ZeroNet) | Xray-core | sing-box | xray-rust | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VLESS | yes | yes | yes | yes |  |
| VLESS Encryption (ML-KEM-768 + X25519) | yes | yes | no | yes |  |
| VMess (AEAD) | yes | yes | yes | no |  |
| Trojan | yes | yes | yes | no |  |
| Shadowsocks (AEAD) | yes | yes | yes | no |  |
| Shadowsocks 2022 (SIP022) | yes | yes | yes | no |  |
| Shadowsocks plugins (obfs, v2ray-plugin) | no | yes | no | no | SS plugin support exists upstream in Xray-core; the other three have none |
| AnyTLS | yes | no | yes | no |  |
| Hysteria 2 | yes | partial | yes | yes | Xray-core carries Hysteria v1 and a Hysteria 2 transport; sing-box and Zray carry the protocol |
| Hysteria v1 | no | yes | yes | no |  |
| TUIC v5 | yes | no | yes | no |  |
| SSH | no | no | yes | no |  |
| ShadowTLS v3 | no | no | yes | no |  |
| NaiveProxy | no | no | yes | no |  |
| Snell | no | no | yes | no |  |
| Tor | no | no | yes | no |  |
| Cloudflared | no | no | yes | no |  |
| WireGuard | yes (AmneziaWG) | yes | yes (endpoint) | yes (bounded) |  |
| MASQUE (CONNECT-IP) | yes (WARP route) | prerelease | alpha | no | Xray-core's MASQUE inbound and outbound are on `main`, not in the pinned release |
| SOCKS / HTTP proxy chain | no | yes | yes | no | Zray resolves upstream proxies from the environment instead of the config |
| SOCKS / mixed inbound | yes | yes | yes | yes (socks) |  |
| HTTP inbound | yes | yes | yes | yes |  |
| Dokodemo-door | yes | yes | no | no | sing-box uses `redirect` and `tproxy` inbound types instead |
| redirect / tproxy inbound | no | no | yes | no | Xray does transparent proxying with dokodemo-door plus `sockopt.tproxy` |
| TUN inbound | yes | yes | yes | yes (fd) |  |
| VLESS inbound | yes | yes | yes | no |  |
| Trojan / VMess / SS inbound | yes | yes | yes | no |  |
| AnyTLS inbound | yes | no | yes | no |  |
| Hysteria 2 inbound | yes | partial | yes | no |  |
| TUIC inbound | yes | no | yes | no |  |
| Reverse proxy / bridge | no | yes | yes (bridge) | no |  |
| raw (tcp) | yes | yes | yes | yes |  |
| WebSocket | yes | deprecated | yes | yes | Xray-core deprecates ws in favour of XHTTP over H2 and H3 |
| HTTPUpgrade | yes | deprecated | yes | yes |  |
| gRPC | yes | deprecated | yes | yes |  |
| XHTTP over HTTP/1.1 | yes | yes | no | yes |  |
| XHTTP over HTTP/2 | yes | yes | no | yes |  |
| XHTTP over HTTP/3 | yes | yes | no | yes |  |
| HTTP/2 as a transport | no | removed | yes (`http`) | no | Xray-core reports `h2`/`http` as a removed feature |
| QUIC as a transport | no | removed | empty block | no |  |
| mKCP | no | yes | no | no |  |
| XDRIVE | no | prerelease | no | no |  |
| none / TLS | yes | yes | yes | yes |  |
| REALITY | yes | yes (raw/xhttp/grpc) | yes | yes |  |
| REALITY ML-DSA-65 signatures | yes | yes | no | yes |  |
| ML-KEM-768 hybrid key exchange | yes | yes | yes | yes |  |
| XTLS Vision | yes | yes | yes | yes |  |
| ECH | yes (client) | yes | yes (no PQ sigs) | yes |  |
| Client certificate pinning by SHA-256 | no | yes | yes | yes | Zray's pinning is a private CA in `tlsSettings.certificates`, not a pin |
| ClientHello fragmentation | yes (`finalmask`) | yes (`finalmask`) | yes (`tls.fragment`) | no |  |
| ClientHello spoofing | no | no | yes | no | sing-box 1.14 `tls.spoof_method`: wrong-sequence, wrong-checksum, wrong-ack, wrong-md5 |
| Private CA for a client | yes | yes | no | no | sing-box has no client CA option; the harness uses `insecure` there |
| Mux | yes (not `muxcool`) | yes (XUDP) | yes (h2mux/smux/yamux) | no |  |
| Mux Brutal | no | no | yes | no |  |
| `packetEncoding` | no | yes | n-a | n-a |  |
| `xudpProxyUDP443` | no | yes | n-a | n-a |  |
| SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE through a proxy | yes | yes | yes | yes |  |
| Outbound chaining (`dialerProxy` / `detour`) | yes (dialerProxy) | yes (dialerProxy) | yes (detour) | partial (TCP only) |  |
| Health checking / balancer | yes | yes (observatory) | yes (urltest) | partial |  |
| Routing rules | yes | yes | yes (rule-set) | yes |  |
| Geodata (`.dat`) | yes | yes | no (`.srs`) | yes |  |
| FakeDNS | yes | yes | yes | yes |  |
| Sniffing | yes | yes | yes | partial |  |
| TUN stack selection | no (fixed smoltcp) | yes | yes (deprecated 1.15) | no |  |
| Management API | yes (HTTP) | yes (gRPC) | yes (gRPC + HTTP) | yes (C ABI) |  |
| Independent security audit | yes (in this repository) | no stated | no stated | no |  |

## Not implemented in Zray

From `caps.ZRAY.notes`:

- Not implemented: `kcp`, `quic`, `h2` as standalone transports, `packetEncoding`, `muxcool`, SSH, ShadowTLS, Snell, NaiveProxy, Tor, SniffTLS, and the `gost`/`sudoku`/`xmux`/`xudp` variants that appear in some panel generators.

## Allowed by the others and not implemented here

### Xray-core

- Not in Zray: `kcp`, `packetEncoding` with `xudpProxyUDP443`, the `finalmask` UDP mask family (`sudoku`, `salamander`, `realm`, `xdns`, `xicmp`, `mkcp-legacy`), the XDRIVE transport, a MASQUE inbound and outbound, `xhttpSettings.sessionIDTable`, and `sockopt.trustedXForwardedFor`.

Known limitations recorded for this core:

- **transports**: Current prereleases report `h2`/`http` and `quic` as removed features and deprecate `ws`, `httpupgrade` and `grpc` in favour of XHTTP. `kcp` still works and is not measured here.
- **protocols**: No `anytls`, `ssh`, `tuic`, `shadowtls`, `naive`, `snell` or `tor` protocol in either direction.
- **reality**: REALITY is accepted only on raw, XHTTP and gRPC. A REALITY server also rejects clients outside `minClientVer`/`maxClientVer`, and the default lower bound is the current Xray version; the generated fixture widens both bounds so the rows measure capability rather than version strings.

### sing-box

- Not in Zray: `ssh`, `shadowtls` v3, `snell`, `naive`, `tor`, `cloudflared`, `tailcat`, `openconnect`, `openvpn-client`, an HTTP/2 transport, a `quic` transport, multiplex protocol selection, multiplex Brutal, TLS ClientHello spoofing (`tls.spoof_method`), a TUN `stack` selection, a `redirect` and `tproxy` inbound, `bridge`, the gRPC API service and dashboard, network namespaces, and a MASQUE endpoint.

Known limitations recorded for this core:

- **transports**: Five v2ray transports only: ws, httpupgrade, grpc, http (h2) and a `quic` block with no options. There is no XHTTP and no mKCP.
- **reality**: No `mldsa65`. Post-quantum is limited to the X25519MLKEM768 curve and the `chrome_pq*` uTLS fingerprints.
- **tls_trust**: A sing-box client cannot be given a private CA, so the generated client uses `insecure: true` against a loopback-only certificate. Zray and Xray-core verify the chain instead, so the TLS rows compare everything except certificate verification.
- **multiplex**: `multiplex.brutal` has no equivalent in the other cores here.
